newsitem.title: UK: Lloyd's appoints regulatory review panel.
newsitem.headline: Lloyd's appoints regulatory review panel.

text.p: Lloyd's of London said on Thursday it had set up a top-level panel to review regulation of the insurance market now that its recovery plan has been secured.
The group, led by the chairman of Lloyd's regulatory board Sir Alan Hardcastle, will look at how to regulate the market as it emerges from the reconstruction process, completed in early September.
Its members are taken from Lloyd's corporate and individual capital backers, plus market practioners and independent experts with experience of financial regulation.
The panel is due to make its recommendations to the Council of Lloyd's before the middle of 1997.
Sir Alan said in a statement that Lloyd's was becoming very different from the market of the past and would keep changing.

"This review, recognising the scope of these changes, will recommend how our regulatory arrangements should be developed in the future," he said. "It is imperative to ensure that the sharp lessons of the past have been properly learnt."
The market finalised a recovery plan last month to resolve disputes over huge insurance losses stemming from an unprecedented string of natural disasters and litigation in the United States.
And an influx of corporate investment over recent years, replacing the traditional individual backers called Names, has changed the structure of the market's capitalisation.
Other panel members include Rodney Galpin, former executive director of the Bank of England, responsible for banking supervision, and John Kennedy, director of the Securities and Investments Board.
The insurance market is regulated under a private act of parliament - Lloyd's Act 1982 - and is largely exempt from the provisions of the Financial Services Act 1986.
